name: Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging
definition: Diversity, inclusion and belonging are fundamental to the success of GitLab. We aim to make a significant impact in our efforts to foster an environment where everyone can thrive. We are designing a multidimensional approach to ensure that GitLab is a place where people from every background and circumstance feel like they belong and can contribute.

rows.situation: When the same few people do all the talking
rows.under: Lets the meeting run itself, and the quiet people stay quiet.
rows.justRight: Asks directly for the views that have not been heard, and leaves room for them to arrive.
rows.over: Calls on people unprepared, and turns inclusion into being put on the spot.

rows.situation: When the team spans many time zones
rows.under: Schedules around the largest cluster, and the rest read the notes.
rows.justRight: Works asynchronously by default, so being awake is not a prerequisite for contributing.
rows.over: Refuses to ever meet live, and the relationships that make disagreement safe never form.

rows.situation: When the candidate does not fit the usual mold
rows.under: Reads unfamiliarity as a lack of quality.
rows.justRight: Checks the judgment against the actual requirements of the job, and separates fit from familiarity.
rows.over: Treats background as the qualification, and the bar becomes unclear to everyone.

rows.situation: When the visible work keeps going to the same people
rows.under: Assigns by who is closest to hand, and the pattern compounds unnoticed.
rows.justRight: Looks at who has had the growth work lately, and spreads it deliberately.
rows.over: Rotates opportunity mechanically, and puts people into work they are set up to fail at.

rows.situation: When a colleague says something exclusionary
rows.under: Says nothing, and hopes someone else does.
rows.justRight: Says it plainly, privately, and assumes good intent about how it happened.
rows.over: Escalates a first mistake so publicly that people stop speaking at all.

rows.situation: When the team's shorthand excludes new people
rows.under: Keeps using it. People will pick it up eventually.
rows.justRight: Defines it in the handbook and in the moment, so nobody has to admit they were lost.
rows.over: Polices language so tightly that ordinary conversation becomes a hazard.
